dependency_constraints.source: inferred from sympy/core/evalf.py diff using mpf_log, mpf_add, mpf_abs; not stated in passages

numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For log(1 + S(10)**-10) near 1, evalf_log loses the small difference (arg - 1) to rounding; 20 + log(1 + S(10)**-10) > 20 evaluates to False and N(x) gives 20.0000000001000, and diff.evalf(2) gives 1.0E-10 instead of the full value at default precision (9.99999999950000E-11). Also log(y/z) with b=1e-22 evalf returns 0 under strict=True instead of raising a precision error.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: x > 20 should evaluate to True for x = 20 + log(1 + S(10)**-10); log of an argument extremely close to 1 should be computed accurately by computing arg - 1 first and raising precision as needed; with strict=True, evalf of log(y/z) should raise a precision error rather than return 0.
trigger_conditions: argument of log is extremely close to 1 (e.g. 1 + 10**-10)
comparison or evalf at low/default precision where the lhs and rhs are sufficiently close
evalf with strict=True on log(y/z) where y/z is close to 1 (b=1e-22)

input_output_examples.expected_output: 20.0000000001000 with the small term retained at full precision (x > 20)

input_output_examples.input: b = symbols('b'); log(b/(b+1)/b).evalf(subs={b: Rational('1e-22')}, strict=True, maxn=1e300)
input_output_examples.expected_output: a precision error should be raised since strict is true

oracle_clues: strict=True should raise a precision error
PR regression test compares diff.evalf() to 9.99999999950000E-11
log(y) - log(z) gives -1.00000000000000e-22 as the accurate reference difference

numerical_characteristics.precision: Default precision and low precision (2 digits) evaluation of 20 + log(1 + S(10)**-10); the passage reports diff with default precision 9.99999999950000E-11 and with 2 digits 1.0E-10. Issue #28514 uses evalf with strict=True and maxn=1e300 on b=Rational('1e-22').
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Argument close to 1: 1 + 10**-10 (PR#28790) and 1 + 10**-9 (regression test); near-1 argument of b/(b+1) with b=1e-22 (issue #28514), where log(y/z) returned 0 versus expected -1.00000000000000e-22 for log(y)-log(z).
category_specific_evidence: Property violated: log(1 + eps) should be approximately eps for small eps, but evalf rounds the argument to 1 at default precision so log returns 0, making 20 + log(1 + S(10)**-10) > 20 evaluate False; the fix requires computing x-1 accurately and adding 1 back at extra precision.
Concrete values: 20 + log(1 + S(10)**-10) > 20 should be True (regression test test_issue_28280); with 1 + 10**-9 also True.
Diff with default precision 9.99999999950000E-11 versus expected 1e-10 with low precision (2 digits) 1.0E-10.
Issue #28514: log(y/z) with y=b/(b+1), z=b, b=1e-22 printed 0 while (log(y)-log(z)) printed -1.00000000000000e-22; strict=True should have raised a precision error.
Discussion notes xre_acc None handling in the accuracy check condition xre_acc is None or xre_acc > 1 is ambiguous.
Diff change removes the re != fzero guard and adds xre != fzero check in evalf_log in sympy/core/evalf.py.
reproduction_risks: The output of the issue #28514 example depends on evalf strict mode raising a precision error, and the passage notes that setting higher output precision avoids the issue.
Issue #28514 and PR#28790 describe different expressions; the 'diff' values are reported as printed strings and may depend on the evalf default precision.
Exact dtype, tolerance, and a numeric expected value for the strict-mode case are not stated in the passages.
